page0.text:
I cut the cod with gusto.
The Napa cabbage is cut and I've grated a ton of daikon radish.
"...All right. All I have to do is put the ingredients in and put it on the stove..."

page1.text:
The pot boils.
It's an easy meal to make, mostly dependent on making the stock.
That went well, so all that's left is to prepare the number of plates needed.

page2.text:
"I'm home! Man, it's so cold, it started snowing."
Fuji-nee comes home.
"Welcome back. It's snowing outside?"

page3.text:
"Yeah. It looks light, but it feels like it's gonna pile up. Wow, we're having hot pot for dinner? As always, you know how to hit the mark. Mm, I'm in a good mood, so maybe I'll drink tonight."
Fuji-nee goes inside the living room, saying dangerous sounding things.

page4.text:
"Hello, Ms. Fujimura."
"Oh, it's Tohsaka. What's going on? It's rare to see you here."

page5.text:
...?
Fuji-nee naturally accepts Tohsaka's greeting.
She hums as she goes past the living room and into the kitchen.

page6.text: "Wow, that's good cod. They say that eating cod while watching snowfall is the best, so it must go with sake even better."

page7.text:
Fuji-nee opens the refrigerator.
And...
After retrieving her favorite Baumkuchen and taking a bite...

page8.text: "WAIT, WHY IS TOHSAKA AT SHIROU'S PLACEEE!!!???"

page9.text:
"Hey, Tohsaka! It's not 'hello,' what are you doing here at this time!?"
Fuji-nee stuffs the Baumkuchen down and marches into the living room.

page10.text:
"Emiya is treating me to dinner. As for you, aren't you lacking a bit of common courtesy to come in without even ringing the doorbell?"
In response, the Tohsaka army calmly makes her counterattack.

page11.text:
"W-well... I-I am the supervisor of this household!
Shi—Emiya's father put me in charge here, so I'm like family!"

page12.text:
"I see. Then allow me to make a formal greeting.
Hello, Ms. Fujimura. I have been spending the whole day here. I will continue to study for an exam with Emiya after dinner, but please do not mind us."

page13.text: "Wha—Shiro... I mean, Emiya! What is this!? Since when did you decide to hold a study session with Tohsaka!?"

page14.text:
"Ms. Fujimura? Please do not push yourself if it is hard to address him that way.
It does not concern me whether how you call Emiya. Whether you call him by his first name or by a nickname, I respect people's privacy."

page15.text:
"Uuuh... Tohsaka, did you hear from Sakura...?"
"Who knows? Unfortunately, it would be improper to say what I've discussed with Miss Matou, since I must respect her privacy. But, I wish it is as you imagine."

page16.text:
Fuji-nee falters at Tohsaka's smile.
...I understand how Fuji-nee feels well.
When she smiles like that, it makes you feel overwhelmed and cornered...

page17.text:
"...I guess the match has been decided. I'll just leave them be."
Actually, it wasn't even a match to begin with.
It's only a matter of time until Tohsaka talks Fuji-nee down.
I'll let Tohsaka take care of it and focus on preparing dinner.

page18.text:
It stops snowing outside once we finish the pot.
It only snowed for about two hours, so I bet there's only a bit of snow left in the yard.

page19.text:
"Shirou, I put the dishes in the sink."
"Oh, thanks. I'll go wash them real quick."
I get up and head to the kitchen.

page20.text:
"The dishes? Should I wash them? It doesn't seem fair if I'm the only one getting treated."
Tohsaka and Fuji-nee switch spots.
The offer is nice, but I can't let a guest do the dishes.

page21.text:
"It's fine, you'll just owe me one. You should rest since you just ate. And Fuji-nee, you go prepare the bath."
"Yeah yeah, I know."
It must be because she's full now, as Fuji-nee is compliant.
Everything would be so much easier if she were like this all the time. Though I suppose it'd also be boring.

page22.text:
"Oh."
I dropped another plate.
It's been twenty minutes since I started doing the dishes. This is the second plate I dropped.

page23.text:
"...Mrgh."
There's no excuse even if my left hand is numb. I'm really dropping the proverbial ball if I'm being a klutz just from this.

page24.text:
...
If I'm being honest with myself, I should stop until my arm no longer feels this way, but I quickly shake that thought off.

page25.text:
I roll up my sleeve and continue washing the dishes.
If this were from something else I could maybe excuse it, but I refuse over something coming from me.
There's no way I'm going to lose to myself. I refuse to admit defeat.

page26.text:
"Mrgh..."
And as a result, the damage taken increases.
This is the third plate now.
Fortunately, it didn't break since I put a bath towel on the floor after I dropped the first one.

page27.text:
So it shouldn't be a problem, but...
...
It's really awkward feeling Tohsaka's eyes on me whenever I drop a plate.

page28.text:
"...Ms. Fujimura. Is Emiya always like that?"
I hear Tohsaka's voice from the living room.

page29.text:
"Don't be ridiculous. Shirou has never broken a plate before. He must be nervous since you're here."
BECAUSE YOU'RE THE ENEMY.
Leave it to Fuji-nee to hit a bullseye on the dig.

page30.text:
...
Tohsaka ignores that and stares at me.

page31.text:
"..."
...This is hard.
Half of my body is already numb, so it distracts me when she watches me that earnestly... Oh, shoot.

page32.text:
"Ugh, damn it."
I click my tongue and look down at the broken plate.
This is the fourth one now. I could see it coming, but my left hand didn't move fast enough.
"..."
I slowly look behind me.

page33.text:
...
...She's watching me.
Tohsaka scrutinizes me from her place at the table.

page34.text:
Then...
She suddenly gets up and walks over to me.

page35.text:
"Emiya. I'll do it, so you go and rest."
"But—"
"Be careful not to step on the broken plates. I can figure out where to put what, so you can go drink some tea."
Tohsaka rolls up her sleeves and stands by the sink.

page36.text:
...
...I don't think I can do anything about this.
It's a herculean task to stop Tohsaka once she makes up her mind, and to be honest...
...It's frustrating, but there's something strangely picturesque about Tohsaka standing there doing something so mundane.

page37.text:
Once I get out of the bath, Fuji-nee is the only one in the living room.
Tohsaka's shoes are still at the entrance, and I assume Saber's in the dojo.
It's almost 9 PM.
Now...
